page: Microsoft Azure B4ps_v2 is a general-purpose, burstable virtual machine powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance provisioned under Microsoft Hyper-V features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs based on the Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware AES cryptographic extensions. Memory is configured at 16.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage, and provides no dedicated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the B4ps_v2 demonstrates mid-tier computational throughput alongside lower-tier single-thread and memory responsiveness. Synthetic stress-ng evaluations register average tier results for both single-core (1822.69) and multi-core (7252.95) execution, paired with average large-block memory read (46.07 GB/sec) and write (29.04 GB/sec) throughput. Gzip single-threaded compression and PassMark database operations also perform within the middle 50th percentile. However, compute tests like Geekbench single-core (1109.0), Geekbench multi-core (3672.0), and PassMark CPU (3208.85) place the server in the lower quartile, reflecting the baseline design of the Neoverse-N1 cores. Cached memory bandwidth and Redis SET operations also fall into lower percentiles.

Because the CPU utilizes a burstable credit-based allocation model, the instance achieves high qualitative cost efficiency during periods of low or fluctuating utilization. The absence of local storage and specialized vector units like AVX or AMX limits its suitability for high-throughput machine learning or demanding numerical modeling, as evidenced by low small-model LLM inference scores. Instead, the balance of 16 GB RAM across 4 ARM cores makes the B4ps_v2 suitable for low-to-medium traffic web applications, microservices, staging environments, build and CI/CD pipelines, and intermittent relational database tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure B4ps_v2 is a general-purpose burstable virtual machine based on the ARM64 Ampere Neoverse-N1 architecture, delivering 4 vCPUs at 3.0 GHz and 16.0 GB of memory. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 32 MB of L3 cache, and hardware AES acceleration. There is no bundled local storage or GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on external Premium Storage for persistent workloads. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance yields average tier results in stress-ng multi-core computing, large-block memory throughput, and PassMark database operations, while general Geekbench scores, Redis operations, and LLM inference speeds place in lower tiers. With burstable CPU credits providing favorable cost efficiency for intermittent usage patterns, the B4ps_v2 is appropriately suited for lightweight web serving, continuous integration runners, dev-test environments, and low-intensity background data processing.
